query: What are the real-world risks and benefits of using synthetic data to train or fine-tune large language models? Focus on data quality, bias, and evaluation.

sub_questions.text: How does synthetic data compare to real-world data in maintaining or improving data quality metrics like accuracy and completeness during model training?
What specific limitations arise in synthetic data generation that might lead to overfitting or underrepresentation of edge cases in large language models?
Can synthetic data reduce existing biases in training data, and if so, what methods are most effective for bias mitigation in this context?
What new biases might emerge during synthetic data generation due to algorithmic design choices or dataset constraints?
How do evaluations of models trained on synthetic data compare to real-world performance, particularly in tasks requiring nuanced understanding of human language patterns?
